AUTHORIZATION.verbatim: Authorize the registry version bump for the model ET fix
AUTHORIZATION.why_it_needed_authorization: harness/wnba_model_v1.py is the pinned source of a REGISTERED model. Swapping it drifted the registry hash and the immutability gate failed the build, correctly. A registered model's source cannot change in place, because past forecasts would then be attributed to an implementation that no longer exists on disk.

BEHAVIOUR_IMPACT_MEASURED.reading: this is NOT a cosmetic change. Rest and back-to-back features change for the majority of 2026 tips, because WNBA games are played in the ET evening and therefore carry a next-day UTC timestamp. Any forecast produced by impl_version 1 used the UTC slice and must stay attributed to it.

REVALIDATION_OWED: the 2026-08-12 walk-forward calibration artifact was produced under impl_version 1's UTC-slice rest/b2b features. Its VALIDATED_VS_BASELINE verdict is NOT automatically inherited by impl_version 2 and is not claimed here. Re-running it is open work.

WHAT_CHANGED.defect: predict_slate computed rest and back-to-back features from tip[:10] — a slice of the UTC instant. A 2026-07-23T00:00Z tip is the ET EVENING of 2026-07-22, so against a last game on ET 07-21 it is a back-to-back (rest=1, b2b=1) and the UTC slice reported rest=2. Same defect class as the wnba_refresh_espn extraction bug: derive the calendar date, never slice it.
WHAT_CHANGED.fix: et_date() derives America/New_York via zoneinfo; predict_slate uses it for both teams' feats lookup
